newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian post, phone workers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Indian post, phone workers call off strike.

text.p: Indian postal and telephone workers on Tuesday called off a week-long strike after the government lifted a ceiling on bonus payments, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
Telecommunications Minister Beni Prasad Varma earlier announced the cabinet decision on the payments, which prompted the unions to end the strike.
PTI quoted O.P. Gupta, head of the National Federation of Telecom Employees (NFTE) as saying that workers would resume duty on Wednesday.
About one million postal and telephone workers in India went on strike last week against a government decision to impose a 3,500 rupees ($100) ceiling on annual pay bonuses.

The ceiling was imposed as an austerity measure by the federal government earlier this year. But the postal and telephone workers argued that a bonus ceiling for railway workers had already been lifted and set a precedent.
Millions of letters have piled up as a result of the strike by six trade unions, three of them representing postal unions.
